title: Penalty lateness threshold must be explicitly defined in system configuration
gherkin:
Feature: Penalty Lateness Threshold Definition
  Scenario: System requires explicit penalty lateness threshold configuration
    Given the penalty system is initialized
    When the system configuration is reviewed
    Then a penalty lateness threshold value must be defined
    And the threshold must be expressed in a measurable unit (minutes, hours, or days)
    And the threshold must be documented in system configuration records
rationale: R102d requires that a penalty lateness threshold be defined to determine when late-return penalties apply. This test validates the foundational requirement that the threshold exists and is explicitly configured rather than implicit or absent.
usedContextItems: Penalty lateness threshold must be defined to determine when late-return penalties apply

title: Return lateness must be compared against defined threshold to determine penalty applicability
gherkin:
Feature: Penalty Lateness Threshold Definition
  Scenario: Penalty applicability is determined by threshold comparison
    Given a penalty lateness threshold of X time units is defined
    And a return is recorded with lateness of Y time units
    When the penalty determination logic evaluates the return
    Then the system must compare Y against the threshold X
    And if Y exceeds X, penalty eligibility must be flagged
    And if Y does not exceed X, penalty eligibility must not be flagged
rationale: The threshold serves as the boundary condition that triggers penalty application. This test validates that the threshold is actually used as the decision point in penalty determination logic.
usedContextItems: Penalty lateness threshold must be defined to determine when late-return penalties apply|Late return penalty calculation
